transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-06
Start: 10:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Carlos Ramirez (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Vertex Head of ML), Ethan Chen (Vertex Backend Eng), Lina Gomez (Vertex CTO)
Artifacts: benchmark_spreadsheet_v3.xlsx (shared), security-summary.pdf (link), runbook-dedicated.md

Topics:
- Results overview (latency/throughput) vs baseline provider
- Tuning: batching, KV cache, quantization tradeoffs
- Next steps: soak test, logs, pricing

[00:00] Samantha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we want to run through the latest numbers we shipped this morning in the spreadsheet. Carlos will walk the results, then we'll surface any questions from your side.
[00:18] Carlos: Hey all, quick note — these numbers are the same payloads you gave us last week, 512 token prompts, mix of short/long, and we've kept tokenization identical. Median latency on Redwood hosted with our recommended batch policy is around 120ms, baseline provider shows ~240ms median. Throughput-wise we saw about 1.8x better sustained RPS on Redwood when KV caching is used.
[00:35] Maya: Okay, that's promising. Is that with KV cache warm? We have a lot of cold-start in our use-case.
[00:44] Carlos: Good call — the 120ms median is with KV warmed for prefixes seen in the set. Cold starts push median up to ~200ms but still generally lower than their median. The p95 is ~350ms on our side, baseline p95 is ~420ms. p99 we're seeing some spikes to 800-1k ms on certain long prompts.
[01:06] Ethan: Do we know what the baseline did for batching? They mentioned aggressive CPU batching in their docs which sometimes reduces cost but increases tail latency.
[01:14] Carlos: Right — our observation is baseline provider batches more aggressively which helps them on throughput but adds to tail. Redwood's continuous batching plus per-request latency SLO keeps the median lower. Also our compile-time kernel selection helps on the GPU path here.
[01:28] Lina: How consistent are these numbers across model variants and quantization levels? We plan to try int8 and q4.
[01:36] Carlos: We ran q4f16 and int8-ish runs; int8 reduces token compute but increased hallucination risk in some evals — quality tradeoff. Performance-wise int8 gave small latency drops, around 10-15%, but batching and KV were bigger wins.
[01:51] Maya: Can you share the spreadsheet link in chat again?
[01:54] Samantha: Shared: https://drive.redwood/benchmark_spreadsheet_v3.xlsx — it's the one you saw, has per-test configs and raw results.
[02:02] Maya: Thanks. On cost, how did the cost-per-1k tokens compare?
[02:07] Carlos: Rough numbers: with our batching and cache it's about 0.7x the baseline cost for Vertex's workload. If you disable KV cache and go fully on-demand, cost delta narrows.
[02:18] Ethan: For the soak test, do you recommend Hosted or Dedicated? We have compliance concerns so Dedicated might be needed for the 48-hour test.
[02:27] Samantha: For true production-like behaviour I recommend Dedicated — same runtime but isolated GPU pool. We'll provision a small reserved pool for the soak so the networking and warm-up behaviour match what you'll see in prod.
[02:38] Ethan: What's the onboarding time to get Dedicated capacity?
[02:41] Samantha: We can spin up a test pool in 24-48 hours once contractual details are confirmed; for a short POC soak we can do a time-limited provision without long-term commit. Pricing will be included in the proposal I send.
[02:52] Lina: On security — KMS, SSO, audit logs — we need SOC2 scope and per-token auditability.
[03:00] Carlos: We have SOC2 and can enable KMS-backed encryption for private deployments; audit logs are available in the Console with token-level tracing. I'll attach the security-summary.pdf after this call.
[03:12] Maya: One oddity — in the p99 spikes you mentioned 800-1k ms, can you correlate those with large batch sizes or GC pauses?
[03:21] Carlos: Preliminary traces show some of the spikes correlate with long sequences and KV cache misses; a few correlate with CPU fallback on the baseline, but in our traces a minority are due to kernel selection edge cases. We'll run a deeper trace during the soak.
[03:36] Samantha: Quick qual question — what's your target latency SLO for production?
[03:39] Maya: 95th under 300ms for our user paths, ideally median <150ms.
[03:44] Carlos: We're within that for most cases with KV warm and the batching policy we recommended; the action is to run the 48-hour soak to see real-world distribution.
[03:53] Ethan: For the soak can you also mirror our traffic pattern? We have periodic bursts and lots of short prompts.
[03:59] Carlos: Yep we'll replay the mixed trace you supplied and include bursts. Also will enable the prefix cache to match production.
[04:08] Maya: About the baseline logs — I'll pull them and share but might need to redact some PII. Is a sanitized log okay?
[04:14] Samantha: Perfect, sanitized logs are ideal. That will help us align environment parity.
[04:18] Lina: Any named competitors we should know about that Vertex is also evaluating?
[04:21] Maya: We're looking at ModelServeX and a managed cloud provider (BigCloud AI) and doing one-off tests with OpenAI Endpoints for benchmarking.
[04:29] Samantha: Noted. We'll highlight where Redwood has wins (latency, consistent throughput, KV caching) and where you might need extra tuning (very long-tail p99).
[04:36] Carlos: I'll add a column in the spreadsheet showing run config vs baseline flags so patterns are easier to see.
[04:42] Samantha: Ok last part — next steps and owners. Carlos will kick off the 48-hour soak (target 6/9), Maya to share baseline logs (6/8), I will send proposal and pricing and security docs (today). We'll reconvene after the soak for results.
[04:57] Maya: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[04:59] Samantha: Thanks, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and the action items.

End of call.
